title: Def-DTS: Deductive Reasoning for Open-domain Dialogue Topic Segmentation

bibliography.metadata_date_caveat: Shortlist has 2025-01-01 placeholders; the PDF front matter states July 27–August 1, 2025. No external metadata request made.

research_question: Can structured LLM prompting that summarizes bidirectional context, classifies utterance intent, and deduces binary topic shifts improve open-domain dialogue topic segmentation across the reported dialogue benchmarks?
methodology: Offline/full-dialogue XML prompting with intermediate preceding/subsequent context summaries, one mutually exclusive intent per utterance, and an intended intent-to-YES/NO mapping. Five TIAGE intents distinguish commenting, answering, developing, introducing, and changing topics; the latter two imply shifts. The inventory and demonstrations change for other datasets. Main evaluation uses GPT-4o on TIAGE, SuperDialseg and synthetically stitched Dialseg711, compared with borrowed and rerun baselines using Pk, WD and F1. Ablations, I/O-format comparisons, conditional binary diagnostics, local-model experiments, cue-word association and model/gold kappa are reported. See evidence_catalog for source locators and topic02.metrics for exact settings. No email/span/overlap/preservation task is evaluated.

key_findings.finding: Def-DTS generates preceding/subsequent summaries, one utterance intent, and a binary topic-shift label for each utterance. The intended output induces contiguous dialogue segments; intent labels are mutually exclusive and are not semantic Topic identifiers.
key_findings.quote: The intent list allows for mutually exclusive categorization of utterances.
key_findings.confidence_basis: Confidence in this bounded evidence assessment; not a probability of transfer to email.

key_findings.finding: In the Table 3 evaluation, GPT-4o Def-DTS reports Pk/WD/F1 of 0.232/0.256/0.699 on TIAGE (100 dialogues), 0.315/0.324/0.686 on SuperDialseg (1322), and 0.015/0.018/0.979 on Dialseg711 (711). It leads the tested LLM variants on all three datasets. Supervised RoBERTa is better on SuperDialseg: 0.185/0.192/0.784. These are dialogue segmentation results, not span or Topic-membership scores.
key_findings.confidence_basis: Confidence in this bounded evidence assessment; not a probability of transfer to email.

key_findings.finding: For TIAGE, the complete method scores better than all reported module ablations, and XML scores better than the tested JSON and natural-language formats. The comparison supports the combined prompt in this setting; it does not show that every module helps in every dataset or that context summaries preserve decision-bearing content.
key_findings.confidence_basis: Confidence in this bounded evidence assessment; not a probability of transfer to email.

key_findings.finding: Tables 6 and 12 measure binary topic-shift outcomes grouped by predicted intent. There are no gold intents, so the reported Acc values are not multiclass intent accuracy. TIAGE row totals yield TP=210, FP=76, TN=1073, FN=105 over 1464 decisions; the recomputed binary F1 is 0.698835, consistent with Table 3 after rounding. Some intent/shift outputs violate the stated deterministic mapping.
key_findings.quote: Since there is no ground truth about intent and only topic shift labels are provided, correctness is determined by whether the predicted intent aligns with the topic shift label.
key_findings.confidence_basis: Confidence in this bounded evidence assessment; not a probability of transfer to email.

key_findings.finding: The experiments use dataset-specific intent inventories and demonstrations. Dialseg711 removes INTRODUCE_TOPIC; SuperDialseg replaces the inventory with question/answer/comment labels. TIAGE examples come from its source paper, while Appendix A.4 says other examples come from a Train split. The record supports adaptation without model training, not a single unchanged zero-shot prompt.
key_findings.quote: so we modified intent pool from original template for each dataset.
key_findings.confidence_basis: Confidence in this bounded evidence assessment; not a probability of transfer to email.

key_findings.finding: The exact preceding window is inconsistent. Algorithm 1 passes max(1,i−2) through i and labels the range through its end; §3.3 specifies −2:−1. Appendix A.1 allows previous/next 1–3 utterances, but its U2 example uses preceding U0–U1 and subsequent U3–U5. The PDF confirms these differences. No implementation window is inferred.

key_findings.finding: The broad claim that every subtask improves performance is contradicted by the sampled Dialseg711 ablation. On the 100-dialogue subset in Appendix B.1, w/o context reports Pk/WD/F1=0.005800/0.008464/0.989770 versus full Def-DTS 0.009024/0.013738/0.982143; w/o all and w/o examples also beat the full method on all three metrics. This does not negate the main full-benchmark result.

key_findings.finding: The preliminary auto-labeling experiment reports model-versus-gold Cohen kappa of 0.485 (TIAGE), 0.429 (SuperDialseg), and 0.975 (Dialseg711). It compares TIAGE with a cited human agreement score of 0.479. No matched model/human study, confidence interval, annotation-cost study, or improved training dataset is reported.
key_findings.quote: Kappa scores of 0.485 for TIAGE, 0.429 for SuperDialseg, and 0.975 for Dialseg711,
key_findings.analyst_interpretation: The numerical comparison does not establish human parity or reliable unattended labeling. The synthetic Dialseg711 score is not evidence for real within-email recurrence.

key_findings.finding: The large local-model comparison uses 100 randomly sampled examples per dataset, not the full SuperDialseg and Dialseg711 evaluation pools. Smaller-model Table 13 scores exclude incorrectly formatted outputs. Its format-error counts and model-specific surviving samples must accompany any performance comparison; the large-model success does not establish suitability on a Raspberry Pi.
key_findings.quote: P _k_, WD, F1 were calculated only for correctly formatted outputs.
key_findings.confidence_basis: Confidence in this bounded evidence assessment; not a probability of transfer to email.

key_findings.finding: The paper aims to conserve tokens while maintaining nuanced topic relationships, but it does not measure summary fidelity, conditions, exceptions, supporting evidence, action scope, approval scope, or reply scope. Boundary improvements do not establish work-text preservation.
key_findings.quote: By summarizing each context range, we aim to conserve tokens while maintaining nuanced topic relationships.
key_findings.confidence_basis: Confidence in this bounded evidence assessment; not a probability of transfer to email.

key_findings.finding: Figure 3 conditions comparisons on Def-DTS correctness: panel (a) keeps only its correct cases, and panel (b) counts shared errors only within its incorrect cases. These subsets cannot establish an unconditional 20% or 40% accuracy improvement. Printed figure counts also do not uniformly match the approximate ranges in §5.4.
key_findings.quote: Figure 3: (a) MATCHED INTENT indicates the accu- racy of the other methodologies for grouped utterances by our intent classification process only in the true cases of our method. (b) MISMATCHED CASE indicates the co-error count of the other methodologies with our methods for only in the false cases of our method.
key_findings.confidence_basis: Confidence in this bounded evidence assessment; not a probability of transfer to email.

key_findings.finding: Table 3 combines borrowed baseline results with reruns. Appendix D.2 reports differences from original results; LLM comparisons use GPT-4o, omit the Plain Text system prompt, and change S3-DST from turns to utterances. Table 15 preserves different original-setting scores. The Table 3 ranking is therefore limited to the stated comparison variants.

limitations: T10-F01/T10-F10: Fixed utterance-level contiguous segmentation does not establish the representation or preservation properties required for msgloom.
T10-F05; T10-I02: Adapted inventories/demonstrations and unclear Dialseg711 example-split provenance limit universal-prompt and leakage claims.
T10-F06: Lookahead excludes a direct claim of online/asynchronous performance; the exact preceding window is inconsistent.
T10-F07: Module benefits vary by dataset; synthetic joins are not natural within-message recurrence.
T10-F04/T10-F11: No gold intents; conditional diagnostic accuracy and co-error plots are not independent intent or overall accuracy evaluations.
T10-F08: Human agreement comparison lacks matched populations, uncertainty and annotation-effort evaluation.
T10-F09: Small-model metric denominators exclude malformed output; no deployment cost or Raspberry Pi measurements.
T10-F12: Mixed borrowed/rerun baselines and model/unit/prompt changes constrain comparability.
T10-F13: Cue-frequency test lacks sample details; the authors acknowledge potentially better intents, example selection and dataset-labeling quality as open issues (§7, evidence_catalog.limitations).
No reported segmentation confidence intervals, repeated-run variability, benchmark contamination audit or near-duplicate controls.

reproducibility.availability_scope: Frozen paper-reported availability only; no present-day network or repository verification. Booleans denote paper resource signals, not independently tested access.
reproducibility.code: Footnote 1 reports public code and prompts at https://github.com/ElPlaguister/Def-DTS; Appendix D.2 says final prompts are attached to the repository.
reproducibility.datasets: Existing named datasets are used; TIAGE is explicitly described as publicly available. T10 does not re-release a new gold corpus here; current access, licenses and exact versions were not checked.
reproducibility.implementation: Appendix D.1 reports GPT-4o, Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct; temperature 0, otherwise original/default parameters; no model-specific tuning or quantization; local inference on 4 NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs.
reproducibility.missing: Dated GPT-4o snapshot, exact executable window semantics, scored sample IDs, explicit metric aggregation and boundary exclusions, local subset seed, complete error-handling policy and API/library versions not specified in the paper.

raw_claims: In the first stage of Def-DTS, we instruct the LLM to summarize both the preceding and subsequent dialogues for each utterance.
We explicitly instruct the model to process this step for two reasons.
For example, given current utterance number is 2, preceding range is 0-1, subsequent range is 3-5.
raw_claims_note: Verbatim source sentences; prompt/list text is source content, not an instruction to this worker.

evidence_family.qualification: Direct dialogue topic-segmentation work; transfer from open-domain/document-grounded/task-oriented dialogue to business email is qualified, not direct email evidence.

annotation_unit.unit: Utterance-level topic-shift/boundary label in dialogue order
annotation_unit.semantic_scope: A benchmark dialogue topic, not an annotated concrete work matter. No comparison of sentence, clause, span, EDU or hybrid units.

prediction_unit.unit: One XML U-element per utterance, with context ranges/summaries, one categorical intent, one YES/NO shift label
prediction_unit.boundary_position: YES marks the current utterance as starting a segment, including the first utterance in the prompt; scoring treatment of the initial boundary is unspecified.

contiguity.gold: Contiguous segmentation as evaluated through ordered boundary labels.
contiguity.prediction: Contiguous utterance partition induced by YES/NO labels.
contiguity.non_sequential_cluster: Not represented or evaluated; recurring content in separated segments is not linked by a persistent semantic Topic ID.

gold.boundary: One binary topic-shift label per scored utterance decision.
gold.segment_membership: Single contiguous segment membership in the evaluated partition; multiple semantic Topic memberships are not annotated in the reported task.
gold.intent: No gold intents, explicitly stated in §5.3.

prediction.intent: One mutually exclusive intent. TIAGE has five classes; Dialseg711 has four after removing INTRODUCE_TOPIC; SuperDialseg has four replacement classes.
prediction.semantic_topic_membership: No set-valued semantic Topic output; binary segmentation does not establish multi-label message/span classification.

gold.within_one_message: No annotation/evaluation of non-contiguous spans assigned to one semantic Topic.
gold.dialogue_or_thread_level: No persistent topic cluster joining separated segments is exposed by the reported boundary gold. Dialogue content could recur, but recurrence membership is not scored.

prediction.dialogue_or_thread_level: Not represented as one semantic object; a later return can at most produce another segment.

gold.scope: No overlapping topic spans, multi-topic utterance membership, or simultaneous cluster membership annotations reported.

prediction.scope: Mutually exclusive utterance intents and a flat contiguous partition; no predicted Topic overlap.

overlap.context_window_overlap: Neighboring context windows may reuse utterances. This is contextual input reuse, not overlapping semantic Topic assignment.

RQ1.assessment: Limited: fixes the unit at utterance; no evidence selecting an email annotation unit.

RQ2.assessment: Indirect only: no email clusters, interleaving or non-sequential topic identity.

RQ3.assessment: No direct support: single predicted intent and boundary; no multi-topic message/span memberships.

RQ4.assessment: No evaluated overlapping/discontinuous Topic representation; context overlap is a different concept.

RQ5.assessment: Boundary and instruction errors are measured; scope/evidence preservation is not.

RQ6.assessment: Strong diagnostic relevance if metrics, conditional denominators and subset scopes remain separate.

RQ7.assessment: Useful transfer caveats: synthetic joins, dataset-specific prompts, incomplete split/leakage evidence and unmatched human comparison.

RQ8.assessment: Suggests controlled prompting/format/boundary baselines and independent preservation tests; no architecture approval.

interpretation.claim: A bounded baseline for offline dialogue-boundary detection is the supported transfer use. The task’s topic-coherence notion can merge distinct work matters or split one matter across segments. Those work-matter errors remain unmeasured.

Bidirectional context assumes access to future utterances. This differs from incremental email collection; a no-future variant must be evaluated separately. Exact-window reproducibility is limited by T10-I01.

A good binary boundary F1 or kappa cannot establish multi-label cardinality, recurring Topic identity, exact span assignment, or scope preservation. Synthetic stitching is especially weak evidence for those requirements.

The measured local-model prompts used unquantized models and four A100 80GB GPUs. The paper gives no arm64/Raspberry Pi cost or feasibility evidence. Small-model conditional scores must include format failures.
